nempe adolescentiam Iosephi, formam, do-
minæ authoritatem, procacitatem & instan-

dam enim impatienter ferunt iniurias sibi il-
latas præter meritum, dicentes: Equidem li-

sem: sed quid mali feci? &c.
2 Ecce autem malitiam & perfidiam mu-
lieris, quæ Iosephum tentauit. Primum enim
oculos suos in Iosephum coniecit: deinde il-
lum sæpe de concubitu alloquuta est: postea
illum est aggressa, & vestimentum illius ap-
prehendit: tandem spe sua frustrata laruam
castitatis assumpsit, & se castam esse gloriata
est falsò, & castissimum Iosephum accusauit,
quasi ipse voluisset eam stuprare: postremò
in causa fuit, ut dominus Iosephi iratus con-
iecerit illum in carcerem, nimium credens
pessimæ fœminæ accusanti, & signa (quæ
sæpissimè fallunt) ostendenti: quemadmo-
dum Fausta Constantini Magni vxor persua-
sit marito suo, ut proprium filium Crispum
interficeret, ut habetur in Chronicis. Idem
vxor Othonis 3. Imperatoris fecit, Maria de

page.notes: The first word of the page, "tæ", is a fragment from the previous line and is kept as printed. The word "Poste-" at the line end is uncertain: the mark after it may be a hyphen or a stray stroke, and the reading "Posterioris" is inferred from the sense. The running head "NVPTIALES." has a decorative initial N and may be imperfectly read. The word "persuasit" is joined from "perfua" and "sit" across a line end without a printed hyphen.
